sources.title: 宿白：隋唐长安城和洛阳城，《考古》1978年第6期，409–425页（注释续401页）
sources.titleEn: Su Bai, Sui–Tang Chang’an and Luoyang, Kaogu 6 (1978), pp. 409–425 (notes continued on p. 401)
sources.supports: Rechecked the supplied scan: printed p. 410 documents only partial surveyed canal sections; pp. 414–416 give Daming dimensions, hall locations and later remains; fig. 6 on printed p. 419 (PDF p. 11) distinguishes ancient reconstruction from modern roads and villages; p. 422 discusses Luoyang markets. The scan repeats printed p. 411 in place of p. 412, so Chang’an fig. 3 is checked in its reproduction in Yau PDF p. 25. Published plans are composite, not a single-year survey.

sources.title: 游學華：唐代長安城建築規模與設計規劃初探，《中國文化研究所學報》17，111–144頁
sources.titleEn: Yau Hok Wa, A Study of City Planning of Ch’ang-an in the T’ang Dynasty, Journal of Chinese Studies 17 (1986), pp. 111–144
sources.supports: Dimensional synthesis citing the excavation reports: 9,721 × 8,651.7 m outer city, 2,820 × 1,492 m palace city, 1,843 m imperial-city depth, 5,316 m Mingde–Zhuque axis. PDF pp. 25–26 reproduce the city and Daming survey plans; p. 30 shows reconstructed canals and distinguishes present rivers. The source does not justify precise citywide ancient canal coordinates.

sources.title: 中国社会科学院考古研究所：《隋唐洛阳城：1959—2001年考古发掘报告》卷1第71页；图版转引于吕伟涛，故宫博物院院刊2021年第1期第79页，图九、十
sources.titleEn: IA CASS, Sui–Tang Luoyang: Excavations 1959–2001 (2014), vol. 1 p. 71; plan reproduced by Lü Weitao, Palace Museum Journal 1 (2021), p. 79, figs. 9–10
sources.supports: Excavation report city plan and ancient/modern overlay, inspected on PDF p. 12. Palace/imperial/east/granary precinct relationships, Dingding–Tianjin–Duanmen axis, southern ward rows, Luo and Chan river corridors. This is a composite reconstruction, not a georeferenced open dataset.

sources.title: 中国社会科学院考古研究所、洛阳市考古研究院：隋唐洛阳城正平坊遗址近年考古工作新收获（2024）
sources.titleEn: IA CASS & Luoyang Archaeological Institute, Recent work at Zhengping Ward (2024)
sources.supports: PDF p. 2 locates Zhengping: east of Dingding Avenue, second ward from the south, with Yiren to its west, Dunxing to its east and Lehe to its south. Excavations identify ward walls, gates and streets, while documenting changes within the ward. Internal courtyards are therefore omitted from this circa-750 map. Text accessed; the repository download was unavailable during preparation.
